prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the continuous receding ground plane of an open-sided pillared parking area, separating the immediate foreground (0.3–0.6 m, white) containing the camera wearer's hands, a yellow bag, and the bicycle handlebars/basket below from a girl in a blue shirt standing 0.7–1.2 m away on the front-left. Behind her and to the right, a woman in a sari stands roughly 4–6 m away (3–5 m behind the girl), flanked by structural pillars and parked scooters at 4–8 m on the right and distant figures beyond 10 m where the background drops to black. Both the camera wearer and the girl—who faces the wearer while angled downward toward the basket—have the handlebars, basket, bag, and a thin curved lock cable within arm's reach, whereas the woman in the sari faces away. Across the five frames, the girl's brightness and scale increase in frames 2, 4, and 5 as she shifts closer to the camera (causing her head to be cropped at the top of frames 1, 2, and 5 and her legs to be occluded by the bicycle below), and decrease in frame 3 when the camera tilts up. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly isolates the thin curved cable in mid-air (frames 1–3) and the continuous distance gradient along the pillars and floor, though it is unreliable inside the wire mesh basket (merging it with the ground behind) and saturates to black beyond 10 m.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete foreground and background entities on a black void, consistently labeling the girl on the front-left (0.7–1.2 m away, facing the wearer and looking down at the basket) and the woman in the sari 4–6 m behind her to the right (facing away), along with distant pedestrians at 10–15 m in frames 1–4. It also segments the camera wearer's outstretched left arm (0.3–0.5 m in front/below) in frame 2 and both arms/hands in frame 5 as separate person masks, showing them reaching into the same 0.5 m workspace that is within arm's reach of the girl. Across the five frames, the girl's mask expands and contracts with camera pitch and proximity—cropping her head at the top border in frames 1, 2, and 5 and her lower body at the bottom—while she raises her left arm to hold the lock cable in frame 2 and lowers it toward the basket in frames 3–5. While segmentation makes tiny distant pedestrians (10–15 m away) and partially occluded background vehicles on the right (4–7 m away) easier to spot than in RGB, it is highly unreliable for objects and scene geometry. Specifically, it completely misses the pillars, floor, and thin lock cable, misclassifies the bicycle basket in frame 1 as a 'suitcase' and parked scooters on the right as a 'car' (frame 1) or 'umbrella' (frames 2 and 3), and merges the wearer's left hand with the girl's mask in frame 3.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D skeletal keypoints for the girl in the blue shirt at 0.7–1.2 m on the front-left, showing her torso facing the camera wearer while her head keypoints (eyes, nose, ears) are angled downward toward the bicycle basket below rather than looking directly into the lens. In frames 1 and 3, yellow arm links and magenta hand skeletons show both of her hands positioned within arm's reach (0.4–0.7 m from the camera) near waist level above the bicycle handlebars, while in frame 2 only her raised left hand skeleton appears in mid-air as she lifts the cable to the right. Across the sequence, the skeleton shifts vertically and changes scale as the girl and camera move: her torso and hip joints are visible in frames 1 and 3, only her raised hand is tracked in frame 2 when her head is cropped at the top, and her lower body joints are occluded or cut off at the bottom across all frames. This map makes the exact articulation of her fingers gripping the cable (frames 1–3 and 5) and her downward head tilt more explicit than the motion-blurred RGB frames. However, the map is very sparse and unreliable overall: it completely misses the camera wearer's hands and arms in the foreground, fails to detect the woman 4–6 m away and the distant pedestrians, drops the girl's entire body in frame 2, and produces collapsed, anatomically distorted shoulder-to-hip triangles in frames 4 and 5.
